methods.label: Factor the difference of squares
methods.explanation:
Factoring the difference turns the search for squares into a short list of factor pairs. Let \(u=m-n\) and \(v=m+n\). Then
\[
uv=(m-n)(m+n)=96.
\]
Because \(m>n>0\), we have \(0<u<v\). Also, \(v-u=2n\), so \(u\) and \(v\) have the same parity. Conversely, any factor pair with these properties gives positive integers
\[
m=\frac{u+v}{2},\qquad n=\frac{v-u}{2},
\]
with \(m>n\) and \(m^2-n^2=96\).

The smaller factor is less than \(10\), since \(10^2>96\). Testing the integers from \(1\) through \(9\) gives all factor pairs with \(u<v\):
\[
(1,96),\ (2,48),\ (3,32),\ (4,24),\ (6,16),\ (8,12).
\]
The same-parity pairs are \((2,48),(4,24),(6,16),(8,12)\). They produce, respectively,
\[
(m,n)=(25,23),(14,10),(11,5),(10,2).
\]
Every original pair determines exactly one factor pair, and the recovery formulas determine exactly one original pair. Thus the count is \(4\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
